context_note: Abstract figure. The 6-8.5% is SHM vs a pooled set of comparators (WHT, CR, CR/CL, CR/HV AND winter fallow CTRL); the SHM-vs-fallow-only % is not reported separately (computed from text values 3.5 vs 3.2-3.28 it would be ~6.7-9.4%, so the authors' 6-8.5% cannot be mapped exactly to CTRL). Only the five-species mix raised yield; single/two-species CCs did not differ from fallow (Fig. 6). SHM effect significant only in drought year 2016, not 2014 (slug-damaged year). Fallow control had no herbicide in winter. Single site, n=4, 2 soybean years, no-till.

Same result as E1 in absolute terms; do not count E1 and E2 as independent effects. CTRL-specific soybean yield only shown graphically in Fig. 6 (falls within 3.2-3.28 Mg ha-1, same LSD group as other CCs). Means across 2014, 2016 and both seeding methods.

Null result: CC type had no significant effect on corn yield (P = 0.063). The value 14.1 is just the lower end of a 14.1-15 Mg ha-1 range across all six treatments incl. fallow; it is not attributable to any specific treatment and should be read as 'no significant CC effect on corn', not as a yield value for CC or for fallow. Corn years (2015, 2017) had adequate rainfall; corn received standard UT synthetic N recommendations.

issue: Not a cover crop vs no-cover-crop effect: compares broadcast vs drilled seeding of CCs (management moderator). Does not answer how much cover crops change corn yield.
context_note: Can be cited qualitatively only: seeding method affected corn yield (broadcast 15.1 vs drilled 14.3 Mg ha-1, P = 0.0004) but not soybean yield.
